'''Brian Dominic MacCraith''' {{postnom|country=GBR|MRIA|HonFInstP}} (born [[Dundalk]], 1957), is an Irish physicist who was the third president of [[Dublin City University]] (DCU) in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. He joined DCU in 1986 and became president in July 2010, for a term of 10 years.  After his term in office, he took up voluntary roles, including the chairs of Ireland's ''[[High-Level Task Force on COVID-19 Vaccination]]'' and ''Future of Media Commission''.

==Early life and education==
MacCraith was born in [[Dundalk, Ireland|Dundalk]], [[County Louth]], Ireland, the son of two teachers, Brian and Caitlin MacCraith. He attended Ballinaclosha Primary School in [[County Armagh]], Scoil Eoin Baiste in Dundalk, and later CBS Dundalk (now [[Coláiste Rís]]), from where he took his [[Leaving Certificate (Ireland)|Leaving Certificate]]. His mother taught him for three years, and his father for one.<ref name="TheArgusDundalk">{{cite web |last1=Roddy |first1=Margaret |title=Second Dundalk man as DCU President |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/argus/news/second-dundalk-man-as-dcu-president-26945808.html |website=The Argus |date=21 July 2010 |publisher=Independent News and Media |accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref> 

He graduated with an honours BSc in Physics from [[NUI Galway]], where he also completed a M.Sc. and a Ph.D in ''Optical Spectroscopy of Laser Materials''.

==Career==
MacCraith worked for a time at [[Dundalk Institute of Technology]], then in 1986 he joined the staff of DCU, teaching in the physics area, and establishing the university's Optical Sensors Laboratory.<ref name="IUA profile">{{cite web |title=Profile – Prof. Brian MacCraith (DCU) |url=https://www.iua.ie/amo-team/prof-brian-maccraith-dcu/ |website=Irish Universities Association |accessdate=22 November 2018}}</ref>  He pursued research in the areas of optical chemical sensors and [[biosensors]], biomedical diagnostics, and [[biophotonics|nanobiophotonics]], and he has published and developed intellectual property in his research areas.<ref name="DCU profile"/> 

MacCraith was, in 1999, the founding Director of the National Centre for Sensor Research (NCSR) at DCU, helping to secure funding of almost 10 million in matching grants from [[Atlantic Philanthropies]] and the Irish government's PRTLI programme.<ref name="NCSR matching grant">{{cite web |title=Grants – National Centre for Sensor Research (DCU Educational Trust) |url=https://www.atlanticphilanthropies.org/grants/national-centre-for-sensor-research |website=The Atlantic Philanthropies |accessdate=22 November 2018}}</ref> He later proposed the Biomedical Diagnostics Institute (BDI), and in 2005, this was launched as a [[Science Foundation Ireland]] (SFI) Research Centre, with the largest quantum of funding for a research project in the history of the Irish state,<ref name="IUA profile"/> and with MacCraith as its first director. He proposed the Nano-bio-analytical Research Facility (NRF) established at DCU in 2010.<ref name="DCU profile">{{cite web |title=DCU President's Office – President (profile) |url=https://www.dcu.ie/president/biography.shtml |website=Dublin City University |accessdate=21 November 2018 |archive-date=10 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810010828/https://www.dcu.ie/president/biography.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="IT2011_Clearvision">{{cite news |last1=Holden |first1=Louise |title=Optics expert with a clear vision for DCU |url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/education/2011/0201/1224288679082.html |accessdate=21 November 2018 |date=1 Feb 2011}}</ref>

MacCraith has also been a visiting scientist at the Naval Research Laboratory, Washington, D.C.<ref name="IUA profile"/>

==DCU presidency==
MacCraith was selected in the search process after [[Ferdinand von Prondzynski]]'s 10-year term as DCU's second president ended, and inaugurated 13 July 2010. In his inauguration speech he commented on the fact that he and DCU's founding president, [[Danny O'Hare]] both came from Dundalk, had in fact attended the same school, and that O'Hare had been an inspiration for him.<ref name="TheArgus_quote">{{cite web |last1=Roddy |first1=Margaret |title=Second Dundalk man as DCU President |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/argus/news/second-dundalk-man-as-dcu-president-26945808.html |website=The Argus |publisher=Independent News and Media |accessdate=16 November 2018 |date=21 July 2010 |quote=...said that having grown up in Dundalk and attended the same school, he was aware of academic achievements of DCU's first President, Danny O'Hare from a very early age. 'For me, Danny was a pioneer, an ever-present symbol of commitment to higher education and the transformation of its landscape.'}}</ref>  He also emphasised the importance of Ireland's east-coast population corridor, and expressed hopes of building links between DCU and Dundalk IT, and County Louth in general, and in 2012, the two institutions concluded a cooperation agreement.<ref name="DkITAlliance">{{cite web |last1=Keogh |first1=Elaine |title=Alliance between DCU and Dundalk Institute |url=https://www.isin.ie/go/news_events/news/alliance-between-dcu-and-dundalk-institute |website=Irish Software Innovation Network (quoting the Irish Times) |accessdate=16 November 2018 |date=23 July 2012 |quote=...in the coming days DkIT and DCU will sign a memorandum setting out areas of co-operation, including academic programme development, research, enterprise support and sharing of services...}}</ref>

Starting with his inauguration address,<ref name="TheArgus_quote_">{{cite web |last1=Roddy |first1=Margaret |title=Second Dundalk man as DCU President |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/argus/news/second-dundalk-man-as-dcu-president-26945808.html |website=The Argus |publisher=Independent News and Media |accessdate=16 November 2018 |date=21 July 2010}}</ref> MacCraith has spoken publicly about the needs of industry and business from the university sector and the funding needs of third level.<ref name="IT170328">{{cite news |last1=O'Brien |first1=Carl |title=What are the must-have skills for today's graduates? |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/education/what-are-the-must-have-skills-for-today-s-graduates-1.3020229 |accessdate=20 November 2018 |publisher=Irish Times Trust |date=28 March 2017 |quote=Employers tell us they want graduates who can solve problems, lead teams, innovate, build relationships and strengthen their organisations”. ... Emotional intelligence is coming up more and more, he says. Digital literacy is also high on the agenda. ... if there is one attribute that looks set to grow in importance over the coming years, it boils down to this: adaptability.}}</ref> He has also spoken on the question of [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] participation by female students.<ref name="SilRepSTEMF">{{cite news |last1=Gorey |first1=Colm |title=Prof Brian MacCraith: Gender imbalance in STEM is unacceptable |url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/careers/prof-brian-maccraith-gender-imbalance-stem-unacceptable |accessdate=20 November 2018 |work=Silicon Republic |date=24 November 2016}}</ref>

==National roles==
MacCraith chaired the ''Strategic Review of Medical Training and Career Structures'', which led to the "MacCraith Report" (June 2014), and later the Review of ''STEM Education in the Irish School System'' (reported November 2016).<ref name="DCU profile"/> 

He is or has been a member of the board of Social Entrepreneurs Ireland (SEI), [[Ibec]] (formerly the Irish Business and Employers’ Confederation), [[Chamber Choir Ireland]], SciFest, the last of which he has chaired.<ref name="DCU profile"/>  He is also Chairperson of the three-member Board of Trustees of the Genio Trust, overseeing disbursal of funds for work in certain areas of social innovation, including dementia and home care.<ref name="Genio Trustees">{{cite web |title=Genio – The Genio Trust – Board of Trustees |url=https://www.genio.ie/about-us/genio-trust |website=Genio |accessdate=22 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="DCU profile"/>

===Future of Media Commission===
In 2020, MacCraith was appointed by the Irish government to chair the Future of Media Commission (FOMC), a commission to study and make recommendations on the future of the media in Ireland, with a particular emphasis on Public Service Broadcasting. The FOMC report was published in July 2022 and the Government accepted, and is implementing, 49 of its 50 recommendations.

===COVID-19===
In November 2020, MacCraith was appointed by the [[Government of Ireland|Irish Government]] to chair its ''[[High-Level Task Force on COVID-19 Vaccination]]'', which oversaw the COVID-19 Vaccination Programme in Ireland and provided advice to the HSE and the Department of Health on the implementation of the programme.<ref name="Covid_TFce_Terms">{{cite web |last1=Department of the Taoiseach |author1-link=Department of the Taoiseach |title=First Meeting of the High-Level taskforce on COVID-19 vaccination |url=https://www.gov.ie/en/press-release/de326-first-meeting-of-the-high-level-taskforce-on-covid-19-vaccination/# |website=Government of Ireland |access-date=18 March 2021 |location=Dublin, Ireland |date=24 November 2020 |quote=The agreed terms of reference are as follows –  1. To support the Department of Health and Health Service Executive to deliver a COVID-19 immunisation programme, that meets best practice and provides good governance, as a critical public health intervention in the prevention and control of COVID-19... 2. ..., etc.}}</ref>

==Publications==
MacCraith has published over 150 papers, and examples of peer-reviewed work include:
* "Novel polymer platform for enhanced biochip performance," Chem. Rev. 2008,  108, 2, pp. 400–422, with Burke, C.S. and McDonagh, C.<ref name="OCS ChemRevs0802">{{cite journal |last1=McDonagh |first1=Colette |last2=Burke |first2=Conor S. |last3=MacCraith |first3=Brian D. |title=Optical Chemical Sensors |journal=Chemical Reviews |date=February 2008 |volume=108 |issue=2 |pages=400–422 |doi=10.1021/cr068102g|pmid=18229950 }}</ref>
* "Novel hybrid sol-gel materials for smart sensor windows," Proc. SPIE 5826, Opto-Ireland 2005: Optical Sensing and Spectroscopy, with Guckian, A. et al.

==Awards and recognition==
MacCraith is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and of [[SPIE]], the international scientific organisation for optics and photonics.<ref name="DCU profile"/>  He is also one of the limited numbers of Fellows of the Irish Academy of Engineering, the body set up by the [[Institution of Engineers of Ireland]]. He has also won the Mallin Invent Award for innovation.<ref name="IUA profile"/>

MacCraith was elected to membership of the [[Royal Irish Academy]], often considered the highest academic honour in Ireland, in 2007, in the Science division.<ref name="RIA">{{cite web |title=Membership Directory – Brian Dominic Mac Craith |url=https://www.ria.ie/brian-dominic-mac-craith |website=The Royal Irish Academy |date=19 October 2015 |accessdate=18 November 2018}}</ref>

In 2014, MacCraith was awarded an honorary doctorate by the University of Massachusetts, Lowell.<ref name="DCU profile"/><ref name="LowellSun14">{{cite news |title=A challenge to 'change the world' |url=http://www.lowellsun.com/news/ci_25787767/challenge-change-world |accessdate=20 November 2018 |work=The Lowell Sun |date=18 May 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
MacCraith is married to Catherine MacCraith, and they have a daughter, Aoife, and a son, Eoin.<ref name="TheArgusDundalk"/>
